search_log: Searched “Stephenie Meyer The Chemist excerpt official first chapter,” “Stephenie Meyer The Chemist third person point of view narrator,” and “The Chemist Stephenie Meyer Google Books excerpt”; opened the authorized TIME excerpt and explicit POV sources.
Searched “The Chemist Stephenie Meyer multiple narrators,” “alternating point of view,” and “epistolary narrator”; found no credible indication of sustained first- or second-person base sections.

Searched Stephenie Meyer's official site for excerpts and opened the author-hosted alternate epilogue PDF; because it is an unpublished original epilogue rather than the novel's constitutive text, it was not used as book-level evidence.
The Google Books result supplied catalog copy rather than a sustained readable passage, so it was not used as person evidence.
person_note: The diagnostic Goodreads passages consistently use close third-person narration, including access to Alex's and another character's thoughts; apparent first- and second-person forms occur only in dialogue or universal maxims. A sustained authorized excerpt independently shows the same close-third technique, while two explicit whole-book descriptions identify third-person narration and one specifies that it remains limited to Alex. Targeted searches found no credible alternating, epistolary, or participating-narrator structure. Coverage does not directly sample every chapter, but the whole-book structural descriptions resolve that minor limitation without contrary evidence.
